analysis.title: First Quantum Minerals (FM.TO): 3Q26 Beat On Trident and Cobre Panamá; BUY
key_insights: First Quantum reported 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of $844M, 17% above GSe ($721M) and 22% above Visible Alpha consensus ($695M). Trident nickel, a faster Cobre Panamá stockpile ramp-up and the Guelb Moghrein shift to gold more than offset a copper and gold production miss at Kansanshi.

FY26 copper C1 cost guidance was raised by $0.3/lb to $2.50-2.65/lb, in line with GSe of $2.63/lb. GS says the increase was already expected from fuel, kwacha and royalty effects, and the company had flagged a $0.25/lb potential impact. Costs improved q/q excluding the high-cost Cobre Panamá stockpile.

FY26 copper production guidance was narrowed to 405-435kt from 405-475kt (GSe 429kt) on lower grades at Kansanshi and Sentinel. GS sees downside risk to its 4Q26 copper estimate of 123kt (guidance implies 99-129kt) and likely to FY27 from continued low Kansanshi grades and the prioritization of acid sales over high acid-consuming production.
GS says the Panamanian government's decisions on Cobre Panamá and Taca Taca permitting remain the key stock drivers, and it expects a positive market reaction to the results.

Cobre Panamá copper production was 13kt (6.6Mt at 0.27% grade, 74% recovery), 37% above GSe, helped by higher throughput after Train 2 started in July. EBITDA was $67M versus GSe $13M. Reported C1 of $4.08/lb after by-products was 16% below GSe. FY26 guidance of 30-40kt was unchanged, implying 14-24kt of sales next quarter (GSe 15kt).

Cobre Panamá has a stockpile of about 38mt (about 70kt recoverable copper) that could support processing until mid-2027. On September 30 the Interministerial Commission gave the President 17 recommendations, including assessing a new agreement that would settle the arbitration and set conditions for a potential restart designed to fund an orderly closure. The President is reviewing it with the Cabinet.

Kansanshi EBITDA was $331M (flat q/q), 13% below GSe. Copper production of 46kt was 5% below GSe and gold production of 25koz was 18% below, on lower grades and recoveries. S3 recovery fell to 80% (2Q26: 82%, GSe 84%) because South East Dome stripping is taking longer than planned.

Kansanshi sold 70kt of surplus acid at $462/t, producing $33M of revenue versus GSe $12M and a $0.14/lb C1 benefit. Management deliberately cut processing of high-grade, high acid-consuming ore to maximize acid sales, and the initiative should continue into 2027. Kansanshi FY26 copper guidance was narrowed to 175-185kt and gold guidance cut to 95-105koz.

Trident EBITDA was $470M (+43% q/q), 15% above GSe, mainly at Enterprise. Nickel production of 9.8kt was 16% above GSe on higher grades (1.3% vs 1.0%) and recoveries (89% vs 85%). Nickel sales of 13.5kt compared with GSe 8.3kt on inventory drawdown. Nickel C1 was $3.22/lb, 8% above GSe on higher TC/RCs.

Enterprise FY26 nickel guidance was raised to 40-45kt from 30-40kt (GSe 38kt), and nickel C1 guidance was lowered to $3.00-3.25/lb from $3.25-4.25/lb. Enterprise grades are expected to decline in 4Q26 per the mine plan.

Sentinel copper production was 49kt (-1% vs GSe) with C1 of $2.7/lb, 3% better than GSe. Sentinel FY26 guidance was narrowed to 190-200kt. Grades and throughput should improve in 4Q26 as mining advances in Stage 2 (In-Pit Crusher 4 completed in October), and the Ball Mill 2 upgrade remains planned for 2027.

Guelb Moghrein EBITDA was $36M versus GSe $10M, with gold production of 16koz versus GSe 5koz after the transition to gold-copper concentrate from August. FY26 gold guidance was raised to 45-50koz from 30-40koz.
Net debt fell $98M q/q to $5,309M, 8% below GSe, and net debt/EBITDA was 2.6x versus GSe 3.0x. Free cash flow was $268M versus GSe of -$393M. Net income was $207M, 35% above GSe.

Growth projects: Taca Taca Mine ESIA approval is expected in 2026 after public consultation in November. FQM will file its RIGI application (deadline July 2027) only after ESIA approval and the water concession. La Granja is awaiting ESIA Terms of Reference approval, with a reserves technical report expected in 2027.

GS rates FM Buy with a 12-month target of C$72.00 against a C$35.89 price (100.6% upside). The target uses a blended 9.9x EV/EBITDA on 2026E and 2027E, with Taca Taca at 0.75x PFS-stage NAV and La Granja at 0.50x PEA-stage NAV. A Cobre Panamá restart is not in the base case.

Key risks: Zambia generates 100% of EBITDA, so asset concentration is high. Also a prolonged Cobre Panamá resolution that limits deleveraging, lower copper prices, a Cobre Panamá reopening on worse economics, and Taca Taca cost, capex or permitting/RIGI delays.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after a 3Q26 EBITDA beat driven by Trident, Cobre Panamá and Guelb Moghrein. The target was raised to C$72 on 19-Oct-26 from C$48 and does not include a Cobre Panamá restart.

sector_views.rationale: GS is Buy on First Quantum, with Cobre Panamá and Taca Taca permitting as the stock drivers. Zambia concentration and Kansanshi grade declines are the main operating risks.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported adjusted EBITDA $844M vs GSe $721M (+17%) and Visible Alpha consensus $695M (+22%). Reported on 28-Oct-26.
3Q26 net revenue $2,086M vs GSe $1,929M and consensus $1,809M. Net income $207M vs GSe $154M and consensus $161M. Free cash flow $268M vs GSe -$393M.
Segment EBITDA, reported vs GSe: Trident $470M vs $407M, Kansanshi $331M vs $378M, Cobre Panamá $67M vs $13M, Guelb Moghrein $36M vs $10M.

FY26 guidance: copper 405-435kt (narrowed from 405-475kt), copper C1 $2.50-2.65/lb (raised), nickel 40-45kt (raised from 30-40kt), Guelb Moghrein gold 45-50koz (raised from 30-40koz), Cobre Panamá 30-40kt (unchanged), Kansanshi gold 95-105koz (cut by 15koz).
GSe EPS: $0.37 for 2026E, $1.44 for 2027E and $1.83 for 2028E. GSe 2026E EBITDA is $2,270.9M, 2027E is $3,691.0M. These are estimates, not reported results.
The earnings call is on Thursday, October 29, 2026 at 9:00am EST. GS will look for updates on Cobre Panamá, the 2027 copper cost outlook given the acid-sales focus, and Taca Taca and La Granja.
risk_factors: Zambia generates 100% of company EBITDA, so energy availability or accidents could limit the ability to meet cash obligations.
A longer-than-expected Cobre Panamá resolution could limit deleveraging.
Lower copper prices could reduce investor interest in owning copper assets.
A Cobre Panamá reopening on worse-than-expected economics.
Worse-than-expected Taca Taca economics (cost, capex) and permitting or RIGI approval and start-up delays.
Lower Kansanshi grades and recoveries, with South East Dome stripping delays, may continue into 2027.
Prioritizing acid sales reduces high acid-consuming copper production and may weigh on 2027 Kansanshi output (GSe 221kt vs 210-240kt guidance).
geopolitical: Panama: the Interministerial Commission delivered 17 recommendations on Cobre Panamá to the President on September 30, including assessing a new agreement to settle the arbitration and set conditions for a potential restart. The President is reviewing it with the Cabinet, and formal communication is awaited.
Argentina: Taca Taca permitting continues, with Mine ESIA approval expected in 2026 after a public consultation in November. The RIGI application deadline is July 2027.
Southern Africa: diesel supply improved during the quarter but prices stayed high, mitigated by lower government taxes/VAT. Zambia's power situation remained stable.

tension_points.bull_case: A potential restart or settlement agreement is under presidential review, and a 38mt stockpile (about 70kt recoverable copper) supports processing until mid-2027. Faster ramp-up produced $67M of 3Q26 EBITDA versus GSe $13M.
tension_points.bear_case: A longer-than-expected resolution could limit deleveraging, and a reopening on worse-than-expected economics is a risk. The recommendations include conditions for a restart designed to fund an orderly closure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A formal communication from Panama's president rejecting a restart, or one that sets worse-than-expected economics.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher operating availability at S3 and stronger acid sales should offset lower grades.
tension_points.bear_case: Lower grades and recoveries are expected to continue in 2027, South East Dome stripping is delayed, and acid sales prioritization reduces high acid-consuming copper production.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 4Q26 copper result against GSe 123kt and the 99-129kt implied range, and whether 2027 Kansanshi guidance of 210-240kt is revised.
